newsitem.title: INDIA: Security tightened ahead of Indian celebrations.
newsitem.headline: Security tightened ahead of Indian celebrations.

text.p: India's northeastern region and troubled state of Jammu and Kashmir were put on security alert on Thursday as the nation prepared to celebrate 50 years of independence.
Separatist groups waging an armed struggle for independence have asked people to stay indoors in most of the northeastern states to protest against Indian rule.
People rushed back to their homes in Guwahati, Assam state's main city, fearing attacks by militants on security forces guarding the city, local residents said.

"For the last one week we are panicky and hope that 50th year of Indian independence celebrations in this part of the country will be peaceful," a police officer in charge of anti-insurgency operations in Guwahati said.

A bomb blast on Thursday triggered by militants about 200 km (120 miles) east of Guwahati was a violent reminder of India's struggle against separatist violence. Seven people were killed and eight injured in the blast.
Six powerful guerrilla groups asked people to stay home and boycott the golden jubilee independence celebrations saying it was the 50th anniversary of bondage under Indian rule.
In Srinagar, the largest city in the Kashmir Valley, soldiers and paramilitary troops tightened security and launched search operations for militants.

"We are facing this violent phase because of the creation of these two countries. We have lost thousands of youth and India and Pakistan are celeberating. It is a nightmarish experience," Manzoor Fazili, a 65-year-old retired teacher and historian, told Reuters.
Dozens of separatist groups in Jammu and Kashmir state are fighting for independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan.

Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in a seven-year-old rebellion which errupted in 1990. Kashmiri separatists and state's cheif minister Farooq Abdullah put the toll at some 50,000.
Kashmir's leading separatist alliance, the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, urged people to observe August 15 as a day of mourning.
The northern state of Punjab was also put on security alert as police feared the disuption of celebrations by separatists.
Elsewhere in India, people decorated cities with lights. Loudspeakers blared patriotic songs.
In Calcutta several functions were organised at the Gandhi ashram, where Mahatma Gandhi spent August 15, 1947 fasting in protest against communal violence stoked by the partition of the subcontinent.
Children from various schools were to take out a colourful midnight procession and assemble at the foot of a statue of Gandhi near the city's business hub.
The chief minister of the northern state of Uttar Pradesh, Mayawati, unveiled a 14-foot (five-metre) statue of Bhimrao Ambedkar, architect of India's constitution and a leader of the low castes.
A hair dressing salon in the southern city of Bangalore offered a free hair cut to anyone who participated in its flag hoisting ceremony on Friday at 8 a.m. (0330 GMT).
